newsitem.title: UK: European LPG steady, Asia weak in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: European LPG steady, Asia weak in quiet trade.

text.p: International Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) prices were stable to weaker in quiet conditions this week, with the market still caught in the shoulder between high winter prices and lower summer levels.

The European market held steady, buoyed by firm naphtha and crude , dealers said. A large propane cargo was reported traded in early April at $192 a tonne cif northwest Europe for early April delivery, slightly up from the levels of a week ago. A trader suggested that the slight increase was not significant.
"It's not really up, but it shows good support for levels in the low 190's," he said.
"With strong naphtha and crude it's not moving down at least." He added that the week's activity had confirmed a stabilisation of prices in the current range.

A butane cargo of 7,000 to 8,000 tonnes was done at $210 a tonne cif UK West Coast, also slightly firmer than the levels seen a week ago but not seen by dealers as indicating a significant change to trading ranges.
In the Mediterranean trade was also thin and quiet. Propane was notionally discussed in the low $200's a tonne cif Lavera, the main LPG terminal in southern France, but activity there was limited.
There was some interest for small lots into Spain, but the market was described as lacklustre.
Propane prices are now so low enough there is no possibility of importing material from either the North Sea or the Middle East into the Mediterranean, a trader said.
Mediterranean butane was also extremely quiet, with some discussion on the small ship market heard at a slight premium to propane, but no activity reported on the large cif market.
But while Europe was largely stable, Asian prices were lower. The last trade heard into Japan was reported done at Saudi Contract Price (CP) -$2 a tonne C+F Japan.
The cargo, of 20,000 tonnes mixed propane and butane, was said to have traded for early April loading and late April delivery, with the discount applying to the April CP.

A full-sized 40,000 tonne vessel of mixed propane and butane, thought in the ratio 3:1, was reported traded at CP -$29 a tonne fob Middle East Gulf, well below recent bid/offer levels of -$25/-$20 a tonne.
